The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=0$ are given in the table below. 

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $4$ | $-1$ | $2$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=0.$ Do not round the answer.

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=0}=$
{{field-1}}

current_example.problem:
The values of functions $h(x)$ and $z(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=-1$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $h(x)$ | $z(x)$ | $h'(x)$ | $z'(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $-4$ | $2$ | $6$ | $3$ |

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{h(x)}{z(x)}\right)$ at $x=-1.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{h(x)}{z(x)}\right) = \dfrac{h'(x)z(x)-h(x)z'(x)}{(z(x))^2}.
$$

At the point where $x=-1$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{h(x)}{z(x)})|}_{x=-1} & =\frac{{h}^{′}(-1)z(-1)-h(-1){z}^{′}(-1)}{(z(-1))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 2-(-4)\cdot 3}{{2}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{24}{4} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
